questions.question: In 606 CE, **Harshavardhana** ascended the throne at which city?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The 'Great King of Kings'

options.explanation: Correct. Harshavardhana ascended the throne at Kannauj in 606 CE.
Incorrect. Pataliputra was the capital of the earlier Mauryas and Guptas.
Incorrect. Vātāpi was the capital of the Chalukyas.
Incorrect. Mānyakheța was the capital of the Rashtrakūtas.

questions.explanation: Harshavardhana ascended the throne at **Kannauj** (anciently Kānyakubja) in 606 CE.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Before Kannauj, the earlier capital of the Pushyabhūti dynasty was ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The 'Great King of Kings'
questions.explanation: The earlier capital of the Pushyabhūti (or Vardhana) dynasty was **Sthāneshvara** (modern Thanesar in Haryana).

questions.question: Who authored the famous classical work *Kādambarī* as well as the biography *Harshacharita*?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The 'Great King of Kings'

options.explanation: Incorrect. Ravikīrti was the court poet of Pulakeśhin II.
Incorrect. Kalhaņa wrote the Rājatarangiṇī.
Correct. Bāņabhațța (Bāņa) composed Kādambarī and Harshacharita.
Incorrect. Dandin was a poet patronised by the Pallavas.

questions.explanation: **Bāņabhațța** (or Bāņa) was patronised by King Harsha and wrote *Kādambarī* and *Harshacharita*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The Chinese pilgrim who travelled around India between 630 and 644 CE was ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The 'Great King of Kings'
questions.explanation: **Xuanzang** travelled in India from 630 to 644 CE to study Buddhist texts and visit sacred shrines.

questions.question: Which ruler stopped Harshavardhana's military advance south of the Narmada River?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The 'Great King of Kings'

options.explanation: Incorrect. Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakeśhin II.
Correct. Pulakeśhin II checked Harsha's expansion south of the Narmada.
Incorrect. Dantidurga was the founder of the independent Rashtrakūta kingdom.
Incorrect. Aditya I was a Chola ruler.

questions.explanation: King **Pulakeśhin II** of the Chalukya dynasty successfully checked Harsha's southward expansion beyond the Narmada.

questions.question: Describe the assembly held by Harshavardhana every five years at **Prayāga**.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The 'Great King of Kings'
questions.correctAnswer: Every five years at Prayāga, after performing sacred rites, King Harsha gave away much of his wealth to Buddhists, Brahmins, and the poor.
questions.explanation: Harsha held a grand assembly at Prayāga every five years at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, distributing vast treasures to religious followers and the needy.

questions.question: Which three powers were engaged in the prolonged **Tripartite Struggle** for supremacy over Kannauj?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: A Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj

options.explanation: Incorrect. These were south Indian powers.
Correct. These three dynasties fought for control over Kannauj during the 8th and 9th centuries.
Incorrect. These dynasties ruled Kashmir, Assam, and Kerala respectively.
Incorrect. They were not the three parties of the Tripartite Struggle.

questions.explanation: The **Pālas** (east), **Gurjara-Pratīhāras** (west), and **Rāşhțrakūțas** (Deccan) fought the prolonged Tripartite Struggle over Kannauj.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In 750 CE, stability was restored in Bengal when the people chose ___ as their first king.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Palas
questions.explanation: According to inscriptions, Bengal's disorder ended when **Gopala** was chosen as ruler in 750 CE.

questions.question: Which Pāla ruler founded the famous monastic university of **Vikramaśhilā**?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Palas

options.explanation: Incorrect. Gopala was the first king who established the dynasty.
Correct. Dharmapāla founded Vikramaśhilā in the late 8th century.
Incorrect. Bhoja was a Pratīhāra ruler.
Incorrect. Amoghavarsha was a Rashtrakūta ruler.

questions.explanation: Pāla king **Dharmapāla** founded the monastery and centre of learning at **Vikramaśhilā**.

questions.question: What was the role of the **dvārapandita** at Vikramaśhilā University?
questions.hint: Refer to Subheading: A university with scholars as 'gatekeepers'
questions.correctAnswer: The dvārapandita was a scholar gatekeeper who tested students before allowing them admission to any of the six colleges.
questions.explanation: Admission to Vikramaśhilā was highly selective; each college was guarded by a **dvārapandita** (scholar gatekeeper) who examined prospective students.

questions.question: Which celebrated 9th-century Gurjara-Pratīhāra king took the titles **Mihira** and **Ādi Varaha**?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Gurjara-Pratīhāras

options.explanation: Incorrect. Nagabhața I founded the dynasty in the mid-8th century.
Correct. King Bhoja was also known as Mihira and Ādi Varaha.
Incorrect. Lalitāditya was a ruler of Kashmir.
Incorrect. Dantidurga was a Rashtrakūta ruler.

questions.explanation: **King Bhoja** of the Gurjara-Pratīhāra dynasty was a devotee of Vishnu and adopted the titles 'Mihira' and 'Ādi Varaha'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The early capital of the Gurjara-Pratīhāras was ___, located in modern Rajasthan.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Gurjara-Pratīhāras
questions.explanation: The early capital of the Gurjara-Pratīhāras was **Bhillamāla** (modern Bhinmal in Rajasthan).

questions.question: Who was the first independent ruler of the **Rashtrakūta** dynasty?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Rashtrakūtas

options.explanation: Incorrect. Krishna I carved the Kailashanātha temple.
Correct. Dantidurga overthrew the Chalukyas in the mid-8th century.
Incorrect. Amoghavarsha ruled in the 9th century.
Incorrect. Pulakeśhin I founded the Chalukya dynasty.

questions.explanation: In the mid-8th century, **Dantidurga** established independent Rashtrakūta rule after overthrowing the Chalukyas.

questions.question: Name the king who patronised the **Kailashanātha temple** at Ellora, and state its unique architectural feature.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Rashtrakūtas
questions.correctAnswer: King Krishna I of the Rashtrakūta dynasty. It is the largest rock-cut temple in India, carved directly out of a single hillside as a gigantic sculpture.
questions.explanation: Rashtrakūta king **Krishna I** had the Kailashanātha temple excavated out of a hillside at Ellora; it is an entire monolithic rock sculpture rather than an assembled building.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Rashtrakūta emperor Amoghavarsha I took on the title ___ meaning 'peak of kings'.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Rashtrakūtas (Page 72)
questions.explanation: Amoghavarsha I was known as **Nripatunga**, which translates to 'peak of kings'.

questions.question: Which 10th-century Arab traveller remarked that Muslims were deeply respected and protected in the Rashtrakūta kingdom?
questions.hint: Refer to Box: Think About It (Page 72)

options.explanation: Incorrect. Al-Balādhuri wrote about the conquest of Sindh.
Incorrect. Sulaiman commented on the Gurjara-Pratīhāra cavalry.
Correct. Al-Masūdī observed mosques and full protection granted to Muslims by the Rashtrakūtas.
Incorrect. Faxian visited India during the Gupta era.

questions.explanation: **Al-Masūdī**, an Arab historian and traveller from Baghdad, praised the Rashtrakūtas for their generous religious protection of Muslims.

questions.question: Who authored the historical chronicle *Rājatarangiṇī*? Explain his distinct methodology as a historian.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Kashmir and Box: Don't Miss Out
questions.correctAnswer: Kalhaņa authored the Rājatarangiṇī. His method involved examining 11 earlier works by former scholars and cross-checking them against inscriptions of temple consecrations, royal grants, and laudatory records, remaining unbiased like a judge free from love or hatred.
questions.explanation: **Kalhaņa** wrote *Rājatarangiṇī* in the 12th century. Rather than relying on unverified legends, he rigorously checked eleven earlier chronicles against royal grants, inscriptions, and coins while seeking an objective, moral assessment.

questions.question: Which 10th-century Kashmiri queen consolidated her authority through tactical alliances, built several towns, and restored temples?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Kashmir

options.explanation: Correct. Queen Diddā ruled Kashmir in the late 10th century.
Incorrect. She was a Vākāțaka queen.
Incorrect. She was a queen of the Bhauma-Kara dynasty of Odisha.
Incorrect. Andāl was a female Ālvār saint.

questions.explanation: **Queen Diddā** ruled Kashmir firmly in the late 10th century, founding towns and building temples.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The 8th-century philosopher Ādi Śhankarāchārya founded the school of philosophy called ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Box: Let's Explore (Page 74-75)
questions.explanation: Ādi Śhankarāchārya taught **Advaita Vedānta**, establishing that brahman is ultimate reality and the perceived world is māyā.

questions.question: Where was the capital of the early Chalukyas, famous for rock-cut cave temples, located?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Chalukyas

options.explanation: Correct. Vātāpi was the prominent capital of the Chalukyas.
Incorrect. Kanchipuram was the Pallava capital.
Incorrect. Tanjāvūr was the Chola capital.
Incorrect. Ujjayinī was linked with the Pratīhāras and Malwa.

questions.explanation: The early Chalukya capital was **Vātāpi** (present-day Badami in Karnataka).

questions.question: Where is the **Meguti temple inscription** located, and who composed it?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Chalukyas
questions.correctAnswer: It is located on the east wall of the Jain temple atop Meguti Hill in Aihole (Āryapura). It was composed by the court poet Ravikīrti.
questions.explanation: The Meguti temple inscription at **Aihole** was composed in classical Sanskrit by court poet **Ravikīrti** to celebrate the accomplishments of King Pulakeśhin II.

questions.question: From which city did the **Eastern Chalukyas** establish their independent rule?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Chalukyas (Page 77)

options.explanation: Incorrect. Kalyāņi was the capital of the Western Chalukyas.
Correct. Eastern Chalukyas ruled from Vengi in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
Incorrect. Madurai was the Pandya capital.
Incorrect. Thane is located on India's west coast.

questions.explanation: The **Eastern Chalukyas** held power in the eastern Deccan and ruled from **Vengi**.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I held the title ___, meaning 'wrestler' or 'warrior'.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Pallavas
questions.explanation: Narasimhavarman I was known as **Mamalla**, after whom the port town Mamallapuram was named.

questions.question: Which natural geographical landmark was accepted as an unwritten boundary between the **Pallavas** and **Chalukyas**?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Pallavas
questions.correctAnswer: The Tungabhadra River served as the unwritten boundary after Narasimhavarman I retreated from Badami.
questions.explanation: Following clashes between Narasimhavarman I and Pulakeśhin II, the **Tungabhadra River** came to act as an unwritten boundary between the two kingdoms.

questions.question: Which famous Pallava port city served as an international maritime trading hub where Roman, Chinese, and Persian coins were excavated?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Pallavas

options.explanation: Incorrect. Debal was an ancient port in Sindh.
Correct. Mamallapuram was a flourishing Pallava port that traded with Southeast Asia and beyond.
Incorrect. Bharuch is on the western coast of Gujarat.
Incorrect. Korkai was a Pandya port.

questions.explanation: **Mamallapuram** served as the prime Pallava port for foreign maritime trade, yielding coins from China, Persia, and Rome.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The Pallava kingdom was brought to an end in the late 9th century by the Chola king ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Pallavas (Page 79)
questions.explanation: Chola ruler **Aditya I** overthrew the Pallavas towards the end of the 9th century.

questions.question: State the ancient capital of the **Pandyas** and name one of their prominent seaports.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Further South
questions.correctAnswer: Their capital was Madurai, and an important seaport was Korkai.
questions.explanation: The Pandyas ruled from **Madurai** and conducted active overseas trade through ports such as **Korkai**.

questions.question: Who revived Chola power in the 9th century and made **Tanjāvūr** his capital?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Further South (Page 81)

options.explanation: Correct. Vijayālaya re-established Chola dominance with Tanjāvūr as his base.
Incorrect. Aditya I was Vijayālaya's successor who expanded the kingdom.
Incorrect. He was a Pallava ruler.
Incorrect. Gopala founded the Pāla dynasty.

questions.explanation: **Vijayālaya** revived Chola authority in the 9th century, founding his capital at Tanjāvūr.

questions.question: Which river basin formed the heartland of the Chola empire and why was it so economically fertile?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Further South (Page 81)
questions.correctAnswer: The Kaveri river delta. It provided fertile alluvial land supported by efficient irrigation systems, ensuring high agricultural yields.
questions.explanation: The **Kaveri delta** was the prosperous agricultural core of the Chola state, bolstered by well-maintained irrigation canals and tanks.

questions.question: What term was used for subordinate tributary rulers who commanded armies and governed territories on behalf of monarchs?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Polity and administration

options.explanation: Correct. Sāmantas were subordinate vassals managing regional administration.
Incorrect. Mandalas were administrative districts.
Incorrect. Bhuktis were provincial units.
Incorrect. They were academic gatekeepers.

questions.explanation: **Sāmantas** were regional subordinate chiefs who supplied soldiers and administered areas under royal sovereignty.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In directly controlled imperial administration, districts were termed ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Polity and administration
questions.explanation: Directly administered lands were organised into provinces (*bhuktis* or *rāşhtras*), districts (*mandalas*), and villages.

questions.question: What democratic feature of local governance is highlighted by the 10th-century Chola inscriptions at **Uttaramerur**?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Polity and administration (Page 82)
questions.correctAnswer: The inscriptions describe the systematic selection procedures and qualifications for members of the local village assembly (sabhā), showing the continued legacy of grassroots democratic institutions.
questions.explanation: The **Uttaramerur** inscriptions explain the election and functioning of village committees (*sabhā*), demonstrating early democratic local autonomy.

questions.question: What was an economic and social outcome of the widespread expansion of royal **land grants** during this era?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Trade, economy and urbanisation

options.explanation: Incorrect. The grants directly established an intermediary landholding class.

options.text: Emergence of non-cultivating landholders and expansion of cultivated tracts
options.explanation: Correct. Landholders often leased land to peasants and cleared uncultivated soils.
Incorrect. Irrigation works substantially expanded.

options.text: Total collapse of cash crop farming
options.explanation: Incorrect. Cultivation of cash crops grew.

questions.correctAnswer: Emergence of non-cultivating landholders and expansion of cultivated tracts
questions.explanation: Royal grants created a new stratum of landholders who often relied on tenant farmers, while bringing new fallow lands under cultivation.

questions.question: What event does the 7th-century **hero stone** at Eduthanur commemorate?
questions.hint: Refer to Caption: Fig. 3.22 (Page 83)
questions.correctAnswer: It commemorates a local chief and his faithful dog who both fought bravely and lost their lives resisting cattle thieves.
questions.explanation: The **Eduthanur** hero stone honours a village chief and his faithful hound who died defending the community's livestock from cattle rustlers.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Commercial associations consisting of traders, artisans, and moneylenders were known as merchant ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Box: Let's Remember (Page 84)
questions.explanation: Merchant **guilds** regulated commerce, managed inland/coastal trade networks, and supported civic charities.

questions.question: Give an example of social mobility during this period showing how varņa was not entirely rigid.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Social life (Page 85)
questions.correctAnswer: Rulers like the Pālas and Kākatīyas were originally classified as Śhūdras, but through political power and governance they gained acceptance as Kshatriyas.
questions.explanation: Dynasties such as the **Pālas** transitioned from Śhūdra origins to Kshatriya status, demonstrating that political elevation permitted upward social mobility.

questions.question: Which professional group of scribes and clerks coalesced into a distinct jāti by the 10th century?
questions.hint: Refer to Box: Think About It (Page 85)

options.explanation: Incorrect. Alvārs were Tamil Vaishnavite poet-saints.
Correct. The Kāyasthas evolved from a professional clerical guild into a distinct jāti.
Incorrect. Sāmantas were feudal vassal chiefs.
Incorrect. Aulikaras were a ruling dynasty of Malwa.

questions.explanation: Originating as scribes drawn from various backgrounds, the **Kāyasthas** gradually consolidated through endogamy into a separate *jāti*.

questions.question: Who was **Tribhuvana Mahādevī I** and what was unusual about her royal title?
questions.hint: Refer to Box: Don't Miss Out (Page 86)
questions.correctAnswer: She was a 9th-century queen of the Bhauma-Kara dynasty of Odisha who ruled with the sovereign title 'Paramabhattārikā Mahārājādhirāja Tribhuvana Mahādevī'.
questions.explanation: Queen **Tribhuvana Mahādevī I** of Odisha exercised full royal authority and assumed imperial titles usually reserved for paramount male emperors.

questions.question: Where is the famous 10th-century colossal monolithic statue of **Bahubali** located?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Cultural life and Fig. 3.23

options.explanation: Correct. The Bahubali monolith stands at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
Incorrect. Mamallapuram is known for Shore and cave temples.
Incorrect. Ellora has Kailashanātha and cave temples.
Incorrect. Daśhapura was the capital of the Aulikaras.

questions.explanation: The monumental monolithic statue of Jain ascetic **Bahubali** was erected at **Shravanabelagola** in Karnataka.

questions.question: Differentiate between the **Ālvārs** and the **Nāyanārs** in the south Indian Bhakti movement.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Cultural life (Page 87)
questions.correctAnswer: The Ālvārs were 12 poet-saints devoted to Vişhņu, whereas the Nāyanārs were 63 poet-saints dedicated to Śhiva.
questions.explanation: The southern Bhakti revival was spearheaded by the **12 Ālvārs** (devotees of Vishnu) and the **63 Nāyanārs** (devotees of Shiva).

questions.question: Which celebrated 6th-century female saint was among the prominent Nāyanmārs?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: Cultural life and Fig. 3.24

options.explanation: Incorrect. Andāl was the sole female Ālvār saint.
Correct. Karaikāl Ammaiyār was one of the three female Nāyanārs.
Incorrect. She was a ruler of Kashmir.
Incorrect. She was a Vākāțaka queen.

questions.explanation: **Karaikāl Ammaiyār** was a renowned 6th-century female Nāyanmār saint devoted to Lord Shiva.

questions.question: Highlight two fundamental contributions made by mathematician **Brahmagupta** in his treatise *Brahmasphutasiddhānta*.
questions.hint: Refer to Subheading: A galaxy of mathematicians and astronomers
questions.correctAnswer: Brahmagupta introduced formal arithmetic rules for working with zero, negative numbers, and fractions, and developed algebraic methods to solve equations.
questions.explanation: In 628 CE, **Brahmagupta** systematised computational operations including zero, negative quantities, and quadratic solutions in his *Brahmasphutasiddhānta*.

questions.question: Which Jain mathematician at the court of Amoghavarsha Nripatunga produced the first treatise on mathematics independent of astronomy?
questions.hint: Refer to Subheading: A galaxy of mathematicians and astronomers

options.explanation: Incorrect. Bhāskara I wrote an extensive commentary on Āryabhațīya.
Incorrect. Virahānka established the Fibonacci poetic meter sequence.
Correct. Mahāvīra authored the first independent mathematical work.
Incorrect. Brahmagupta covered astronomy along with mathematics.

questions.explanation: The 9th-century mathematician **Mahāvīra** separated mathematical treatises from purely astronomical studies.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The Hūņa invaders were defeated in the early 6th century by King Yashodharma of the ___ dynasty.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Hūņas' challenge and Fig. 3.25
questions.explanation: King Yashodharma of the **Aulikara** dynasty from Daśhapura checked and halted the Hūņa incursions.

questions.question: Mention two ways in which the **Hūņas** assimilated into mainstream Indian society by the 7th century.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Hūņas' challenge (Page 90)
questions.correctAnswer: They adopted Sanskrit and Prakrit for their records, used Gupta-style coin designs with Hindu symbols (like Lakshmi or Shiva), and served in local army and temple councils.
questions.explanation: Rather than remaining distinct outsiders, the **Hūņas** integrated by adopting Indian scripts, honoring Hindu gods on their coins, and participating in civil governance.

questions.question: Who led the Arab expedition that conquered Debal and defeated King Dahar of Sindh in 712 CE?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Arabs arrive on India's shores

options.explanation: Correct. Muhammad bin Qasim commanded the Syrian and Iraqi Arab forces in Sindh.
Incorrect. Bakhtiyar Khilji raided centuries later.
Incorrect. Al-Masūdī was an explorer and chronicler.
Incorrect. Sulaiman was a merchant traveller.

questions.explanation: **Muhammad bin Qasim** captured the port of Debal and defeated King Dāhar at Aror in 712 CE.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The 13th-century Persian chronicle that details the Arab conquest of Sindh is called the ___.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Arabs arrive on India's shores
questions.explanation: The ***Chachnāma*** provides a historical account of Muhammad bin Qasim's expedition and King Dahar's defense.

questions.question: Which Gurjara-Pratīhāra king is celebrated in a Gwalior inscription for defeating a large Arab ('Mlechchha') army?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Arabs arrive on India's shores (Page 92)
questions.explanation: The Gwalior inscription records that Pratīhāra ruler **Nāgabhața I** decisively checked Arab incursions into western India.

questions.question: Why did Arab governors eventually modify their policy towards Hindus and Buddhists in Sindh after the initial conquest?
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Arabs arrive on India's shores (Page 92)

options.text: They were forced by continuous local resistance and political practicality to allow temple worship
options.explanation: Correct. They permitted native religious practices and temple upkeep to maintain administration.

options.text: They completely abandoned the conquered territories immediately
options.explanation: Incorrect. They retained petty principalities in Sindh and Multan.
Incorrect. They remained Muslims.

options.text: All inhabitants fled across the Himalayas
options.explanation: Incorrect. Society continued with local compromises.

questions.correctAnswer: They were forced by continuous local resistance and political practicality to allow temple worship
questions.explanation: Due to fierce Indian counter-offensives and administrative necessity, Arab rulers allowed local subjects to rebuild shrines and retain temple revenues.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The English word 'monsoon' originates from the Arabic word ___, meaning 'season'.
questions.hint: Refer to Section: The Arabs arrive on India's shores (Page 93)
questions.explanation: The term monsoon comes from the Arabic word **mawsim**, which signifies the seasonal prevailing winds.

questions.question: How did Indian decimal mathematics and numerals reach Europe during the medieval period?
questions.hint: Refer to Box: Don't Miss Out (Page 93)
questions.correctAnswer: Sanskrit texts on mathematics and zero were translated into Arabic in Baghdad, and the Arabs subsequently transmitted this numbering system to Europe.
questions.explanation: Indian decimal numerals with the zero concept were translated in Baghdad and disseminated across the Mediterranean, becoming known as **Hindu-Arabic numerals**.

questions.question: Match the ruling dynasty or king in **Column A** with their respective capital or centre in **Column B**.
questions.hint: Refer to Activity 7 (Page 96) and Chapter Maps
questions.explanation: The Rāşhtrakūtas ruled from Mānyakheța, the Cholas from Tanjāvūr, and Harshavardhana ruled from Kānyakubja (Kannauj).

questions.question: Match the celebrated author/scholar in **Column A** with their famous work or monument in **Column B**.
questions.hint: Refer to Sections on Literature, Kashmir, and Sciences
questions.explanation: Kalhaņa authored *Rājatarangiṇī*, Brahmagupta composed *Brahmasphutasiddhānta*, and Rashtrakūta king Krishna I created the Kailashanātha temple.
